title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Organizational messages can be delivered by email
summary: The briefing's controls, rollout facts and licensing caveats are supported. One clarification remains: the organizational messages guide lists eight email templates, while Microsoft's June release notes describe nine, including Welcome to Copilot Trial.

claims.claim: Organizational messages now supports email in addition to its existing Windows and Teams surfaces.
claims.quote: Organizational Messages now includes Email as a delivery channel, expanding beyond existing surfaces such as the Windows Taskbar, Windows Notifications, Windows Spotlight, and Teams Popovers.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is May CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "May CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is November CY2025.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "November CY2025"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phases are General Availability and Preview.

claims.claim: The Location step offers Windows Spotlight, taskbar, Notification Center, Microsoft Teams and email.
claims.quote: Location: When you create an organizational message, you can choose where your message is displayed to users. Supported locations include Windows Spotlight, the taskbar, Notification Center, Microsoft Teams and email.

claims.claim: The organizational messages guide lists two welcome templates named Welcome to Copilot and Welcome to Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Two welcome messages for Welcome to Copilot and Welcome to Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Six templates come from the Great Microsoft Copilot Journey and address Copilot onboarding and adoption.
claims.quote: Six templates from the Great Microsoft Copilot Journey that highlight features and best practices to help drive Copilot onboarding and adoption.

claims.quote: Selecting a pre-made message doesn't require any approval before the message can be delivered to end users.

claims.quote: Approvers must approve custom messages before the system delivers them to users.

claims.claim: The Copilot release notes list organizational message email delivery among updates released between May 19 and June 2, 2026.
claims.quote:
Updates released between May 19, 2026, June 2, 2026
Organizational Messages now supports Email messages

claims.quote: No, government environments such as GCC or GCC-H aren't supported at this time.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The documented Windows tenant policies and Intune delivery settings are not needed for email.
claims.quote: Set tenant policies only if you need to deliver messages to Windows surfaces such as Windows Spotlight, Windows Notification Center, and Windows Taskbar. You don't need to set tenant policies for sending messages to Teams Teaching notifications or to Email.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls notes
claims.claim: Creating organizational messages requires the Organizational Messages Writer Microsoft Entra role.
claims.quote: Assign the Organizational Messages Writer role in the Microsoft 365 admin center to anyone in your organization who wants to create messages. To access the organizational messages experiences, you need the Organizational Messages Writer Microsoft Entra role.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Email delivery is admin-opt-in through role assignment and a Writer creating and scheduling a message.
claims.quote:
Authors - Assign the Organizational Messages Writer role in the Microsoft 365 admin center to anyone in your organization who wants to create messages.
Finish: Review the message before scheduling or sending for approval by your organization's approvers.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that this organizational message email feature sends messages without an author creating and scheduling them.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "email" "automatically" enabled default; read organizational messages guide and FAQ. The Copilot enable-users result describes a separate automatic license-assignment notification, not automatic sends from this wizard.

claims.claim: The Schedule step configures start date, end date and frequency.
claims.quote: Schedule: Configure the start date, end date, and frequency when the message is sent to users.

claims.claim: Urgent messages support only Windows 11 Taskbar and Notifications area, not email.
claims.quote: The only locations available are Windows 11 Taskbar and Notifications area.

claims.claim: An administrator can cancel a message before or during delivery.
claims.quote: Canceled - An admin stopped and canceled the message. The cancellation could be either prior or during the delivery of the message.

claims.quote:
any message configured to be delivered to a Windows channel, like Windows Spotlight or Taskbar requires that recipients use Windows 11, version 25H2 and 24H2 Enterprise.
Devices - (For Windows)

Windows Enterprise E3 or E5 license.

claims.claim: The FAQ says pre-made messages might remain available without those licences.

claims.claim: Recipients do not need a Microsoft Entra role to receive organizational messages.
claims.quote: end users aren't required to have any Microsoft Entra roles to receive organizational messages.

claims.claim: Recipients must have access to the Microsoft products configured for message delivery.
claims.quote: Recipients must have access to the Microsoft products the messages are configured for delivery.

claims.claim: Available targeting options depend on the message location.
claims.quote: The available targeting options depend on the message location you select.

claims.claim: The documentation does not enumerate which targeting options are available specifically for email.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "email" "targeting"; organizational messages email default enabled automatically admin enable targeting groups. Read guide Create a new message and advanced-targeting sections, FAQ and June 2 release-note excerpts; no email-specific option list.

claims.claim: The Recipients step selects organizational groups to receive a message.
claims.quote: Recipients: Set the groups within your organization that should receive the message.

claims.claim: The Writer assignment path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Show all > Users > Active users > user > Roles > Manage roles > Admin center access > Show all by category > Other > Organizational Messages Writer.
claims.quote:
In the user's details pane, select Manage roles under Roles.
In the Manage admin roles pane, select Admin center access, and then select Show all by category.
Scroll down to the Other section.
In the Other section, select the checkbox next to Organizational Messages Writer

From Manage messages, your team can perform the following actions on messages:

claims.claim: Active is a message status for messages currently being delivered.
claims.quote: Active - Message is currently being delivered to your users.

claims.claim: Completed is a message status for successful delivery as defined by the start and end dates.
claims.quote: Completed - The message successfully was delivered as defined by start and end dates.

claims.claim: Failed is a message status when the service could not properly register the message.
claims.quote: Failed - The organizational messages service wasn't able to properly register the message.

claims.where: Governance controls: Allow Microsoft messages to display

claims.quote:
In the Settings pane, deselect the option Allow Microsoft messages to display.
These steps ensure the Organizational messages platform sends only your organization's messages to Windows surfaces.
